extracted.intended_audience: Competent Authorities of Contracting Parties to the Lisbon Agreement, WIPO Secretariat, and Lisbon Union delegates/administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed amendments to the Common Regulations under the Lisbon Agreement and the Geneva Act governing definitions, fees, permissible modifications and corrections in the International Register for appellations of origin and geographical indications. The document sets substantive procedural and legal rules that Contracting Parties and the International Bureau must apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Official Form' (Rule 1(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Official Form" means a form drawn up by the International Bureau or an electronic interface made available by the International Bureau on the website of the Organization;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends the definition of "official form" to expressly include an electronic interface (e-Lisbon). Purpose: to recognise electronic filing/interface as an official form for the Lisbon System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee applicable where fee changes after filing (Rule 8(9)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of the fees payable in respect of an application referred to in Rule 5(2)(c) is changed between the date of filing the application and the date of payment, the fee that was valid on the first date shall be applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines that for applications (Rule 5(2)(c)) the fee in force on the filing date applies even if fees change before payment; rationale: predictability and equal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee applicable for requests to enter a modification (Rule 8(9)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of the fees payable in respect of a request for entry of a modification referred to in Rule 15(2)(a) is changed between the date on which the request was presented and the date of payment, the fee that was valid on the first date shall be applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For requests to record modifications under Rule 15(2)(a), the fee in force on the presentation date applies; ensures certainty for users filing modification requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee applicable for fees tied to entry into force of Geneva Act for States party to 1967 Act (Rule 8(9)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of the fees to be paid in relation to a modification or as an individual fee, in the case referred to in Rule 7(4)(a) and (d), is changed between the date of entry into force of the Geneva Act with respect to a State that is party to the 1967 Act and the date of payment, the fee that was valid on the first date shall be applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that for the transitional case tied to the Geneva Act entry into force for certain States, the fee in force on that entry-into-force date applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee applicable where none of the specific exceptions apply (Rule 8(9)(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amount of any fee other than the fees referred to in subparagraphs (a), (b) and (c) is changed, the amount valid on the date on which the fee was received by the International Bureau shall be applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default rule: for all other fees, the amount in force on the date the International Bureau actually receives the fee governs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible modification: modification relating to the appellation or geographical indication (Rule 15(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: (vii) a modification relating to the appellation of origin or the geographical indication;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates one category of modifications that may be recorded in the International Register; such modifications may trigger the notification/refusal procedures set out in Rule 15(5) and Rules 9–12 (mutatis mutandis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible modification: modification relating to the good or goods (Rule 15(1)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: (viii) a modification relating to the good or goods to which the appellation of origin or the geographical indication applies;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that changes to the product(s) covered by the appellation/geographical indication are permissible modifications that may be recorded; such changes can be subject to Competent Authority declarations under Rule 15(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible modification: modification relating to listed particulars (Rule 15(1)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: (ix) a modification relating to the particulars as referred to in Rule 5(3)(a) or the information referred to in Rule 5(6)(a)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows recording of modifications to specified particulars or information (per Rule 5 provisions); such modifications may lead to Competent Authority notifications/refusals under Rule 15(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent Authority right to declare inability to ensure protection for modifications to appellation/goods (Rule 15(5)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the modification concerns the appellation of origin or the geographical indication, or the good or goods to which the appellation of origin or the geographical indication applies, the Competent Authority of a Contracting Party has the right to declare that it cannot ensure the protection of the appellation of origin or geographical indication because of the modification. The declaration shall be addressed to the International Bureau by such Competent Authority within a period of one year from the date of receipt of the notification by the International Bureau of the modification. Rules 9 to 12 shall apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants a one-year window for Competent Authorities to object (declare inability to ensure protection) when modifications affect the appellation or covered goods; objections follow the procedures in Rules 9–12 adapted as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent Authority right to declare inability to ensure protection for modifications to particulars (Rule 15(5)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the modification concerns the particulars as referred to in Rule 5(3)(a), the Competent Authority of a Contracting Party that has made the notification under Rule 5(3), has the right to declare that it cannot ensure the protection of the appellation of origin or geographical indication because of the modification. The declaration shall be addressed to the International Bureau by such Competent Authority within a period of one year from the date of receipt of the notification by the International Bureau of the modification. Rules 9 to 12 shall apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits a Competent Authority that originally made the particulars notification under Rule 5(3) to object within one year to modifications to those particulars; objections proceed under Rules 9–12 adapted accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent Authority right to declare inability to ensure protection after correction (Rule 18(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the correction of an error concerns the appellation of origin or the geographical indication, or the good or goods to which the appellation of origin or the geographical indication applies, the Competent Authority of a Contracting Party has the right to declare that it cannot ensure the protection of the appellation of origin or geographical indication after because of the correction. The declaration shall be addressed to the International Bureau by such Competent Authority within a period of one year from the date of receipt of the notification by the International Bureau of the correction. Rules 9 to 12 shall apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors Rule 15(5): grants Competent Authorities a one-year period to declare they cannot ensure protection following a correction to the International Register when that correction affects the appellation or goods; objections follow Rules 9–12 adapted as necessary. Clarifies that a refusal following a correction can only be based on that correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of entry into force for the proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Working Group recommended that the proposed amendments to Rules 1, 8, 15 and 18 of the Common Regulations, as reproduced in the Annex to the present document, enter into force on July 1, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the recommended effective date for the amendments, which determines when the new definitions, fee-rules, modification and correction procedures will apply.
